title: The deal: one retreat from two sides
description: The core of the course. Who is responsible for what, contract models, one deal in the calculator, a price from the profit you want, and cash over time.

units.title: First the profit you want, then the price

objectives.text: For each of the four contract models, name who pays for empty places
Tell "profit" as the venue counts it from the leader's honest profit and find break-even in guests
Derive the price from a target profit, hours of preparation and every line of the leader's costs
Find the cash gap by month and name the levers that close it

checks.question: A full campus of 16 places, 12 guests came. Who pays for the four empty places?
options: The venue: it failed to fill the campus itself
The leader: with a full campus the contract is counted on the whole capacity
Half each: that is the custom in group contracts
Nobody: empty places are simply not paid for
checks.explain: In the "full campus" model the leader pays the rate for every place on the campus, however many guests come. Empty places are their cost (u1, "Four contract models").

checks.question: Why is "profit" as the venue counts it bigger than the leader's honest profit?
options: The venue inflates the numbers to sell the campus
The venue does not count the leader's costs and empty places: it only sees the markup over the rate
Honest profit includes taxes and the venue's profit does not
It is a rounding error in the calculator
checks.explain: The venue counts (price − rate) × guests. The leader's costs — card fees, flights, gifts — and empty places are not in that formula (u2, "Two profits").

checks.question: In what order does the course suggest arriving at a retreat price?
options: Look at prices of similar retreats and go a little below
Take the venue rate and add a fixed markup
Set the profit you want, gather all the costs, and only then derive the price
Set the price and count the profit after the retreat
checks.explain: The price is derived from the profit and every cost line, including the forgotten ones: flights, phone, photographer, gifts. Someone else's price says nothing about your lines (u3, "The reverse order").

checks.question: The retreat is profitable, but in the third month the account is negative. Which of these closes the gap?
options: Raise the price: profit grows and the gap disappears
A bigger first guest payment and booking the venue after the minimum of deposits
Nothing: a gap is a normal part of any retreat
Move the retreat a year later
checks.explain: A gap is about the order of payments, not the size of profit. It is closed by guests' money arriving before the venue payments (u4, "What closes the gap").
